title: {{NAME}} and the Unicorn Crown
moral: Some gifts are only given to those who know they don't need them.

pages.content:
Every hundred years, a unicorn appeared in the kingdom and chose a companion.

The choosing was an enormous ceremony. Every princess, every noble, every important person in the kingdom stood in a long line in the palace meadow while the unicorn walked past.

{{NAME}} was there as a page, which meant he stood at the very end holding the refreshment tray.

The unicorn walked the whole line. Past the princess. Past the nobles. Past everyone.

Then it walked to the end, looked at {{NAME}}, and sat down.

pages.content:
There was considerable confusion.

{{NAME}} was confused. The assembled royalty were confused. The royal unicorn scholar was very confused and consulting several books at once.

Princess Adelaide was not confused. She watched the unicorn watching {{NAME}} and nodded slowly.

"It's never been wrong," she said quietly.

"But I'm just a page," said {{NAME}}.

"The unicorn doesn't know that," said the princess. "Or more likely, doesn't care."

pages.content:
The unicorn's name was Comet and she was, he discovered, absolutely sure about her decision.

She followed him to his small page's room and stood in the doorway, which was too small for her, so she waited outside while he moved things around.

She walked beside him on his errands. She stood outside the kitchens while he fetched bread. She waited outside the library while he returned books.

By the third day, he had stopped questioning it and started talking to her, which seemed to be all she'd wanted.

pages.content:
The unicorn scholar told him the ceremony: in accepting the companion bond, he would receive the Unicorn Crown, a circlet of silver and magic.

"What does it do?" {{NAME}} asked.

"It means the unicorn trusts you completely," said the scholar. "The magic it grants is different for each companion."

Comet lowered her head and the crown appeared, simple and glowing.

{{NAME}} put it on. For a moment he saw through Comet's eyes: the meadow vast and green, himself small and kind-faced, trustworthy.

"Oh," he said quietly. "I see."

pages.content:
Princess Adelaide found him in the meadow that evening, sitting with Comet's head resting in his lap.

"How do you feel?" she asked.

"Like myself," said {{NAME}}. "Just more sure of it."

The princess smiled. "That is exactly what the crown does. It reflects what's already there."

He walked home later with the crown in his pocket, warm and small, and Comet standing at the meadow's edge watching him go.

In his room that night, he set the crown on his windowsill and fell asleep with moonlight on his face, full of a quiet certainty he had no name for.
